clue.text: They'll lay out actions beside logic, primarily

definitions.text: They'll lay out actions beside logic, primarily

indicators.note: to lay out is to arrange afresh, so the letters of the two words before it are set out in a new order
primarily means at first, so only the opening letter of logic is used

explanation.surface: A description of some system or document that sets out what to do alongside its reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay out' is the anagram signal and 'primarily' takes the opening letter of logic. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: tables that set out which actions follow from which logical conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: These are grids used in programming and analysis that map combinations of conditions to the actions to take.

clue.text: Operating system's sound: these people are unproductive

indicators.note: the word sound tells us to go by how the operating system's name is pronounced

parts.note: Unix is a computer operating system; with the possessive it is said like the answer

explanation.surface: A grumble that a computer system's noise comes from staff who get nothing done.
explanation.walkthrough: Unix's, said out loud, matches the answer. 'sound' looks like a noun about the machine's hum but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated men cannot father children, so they are unproductive in the reproductive sense.

clue.text: Number one song Elton possibly put in note, all about being trashed

indicators.note: about signals turning round, and all says the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the song and the comedian are placed inside the note

parts.note: TI is a variant of te, a note of the sol-fa scale
an air is a song or tune
Ben Elton is a British comedian and writer, so Elton may be Ben

explanation.surface: Elton John's chart-topper is slipped into a message, apparently all about getting wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elton' looks like Elton John but is the comedian Ben Elton. 'put in' is the container signal and 'all about' reverses the whole assembly, NOITAIRBENI.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed is slang for very drunk, and this is the formal noun for the state of drunkenness.

clue.text: Think cerebrally elite Latin clues are tortuous

indicators.note: tortuous means twisting, so the letters of the three words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that clever-clever Latin crossword clues are needlessly convoluted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are tortuous' rearranges ELITE LATIN CLUES, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: To intellectualise is to treat something in a purely rational, cerebral way, i.e. to think about it abstractly.

clue.text: Limited view of expression of relief in tidy flush, exchanging queen and first of tens

indicators.note: the expression of relief sits inside the other pieces
exchanging tells us the queen letter and the tens letter swap places

parts.note: neat means tidy
redness is the flush of a blushing face
R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of tens

parts.note: a sigh is a breath of relief

explanation.surface: An odd scene: a sigh of relief in a neat flush of cards, with a queen swapped for a ten.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT REDNESS holds T then R; 'exchanging' swaps the queen R and T, the 'first of tens', giving NEAR TEDNESS, and SIGH goes 'in' the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sightedness means seeing only what is close, so the field of clear vision is limited.

clue.text: Clinton's behind Democratic mascot

definitions.meaning: in American slang the backside, which an American politician like Clinton has
the donkey symbol of the US Democratic Party

explanation.surface: A US political gag: Clinton is backing the party's animal emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The American word for bottom, and the animal (a donkey) that stands for the Democratic Party.

clue.text: Fail to cover fine before energy inspection

indicators.note: before puts the first assembly ahead of the energy letter
the word for fail goes over and around the word for fine

parts.note: to lose is to fail, as a contest
OK means fine
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone fails to pay a fine ahead of an energy-efficiency inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' is the container signal, giving LOOKSE, and 'before' sets that ahead of the energy symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal phrase for a quick glance or survey of something, i.e. a brief inspection.

clue.text: Eject leader from safe seat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from safe

parts.note: a pew is a church seat

explanation.surface: A political party throws its leader out of a constituency they were sure to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'safe seat' reads as a sure-thing constituency, but it splits: S from 'safe' and PEW for 'seat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to throw out or vomit forth, a forceful way to expel something.

clue.text: Cable-supporting sphere?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
Vince Cable was a British Liberal Democrat leader and minister

explanation.surface: A puzzling engineering term for a globe that holds up cables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cable-supporting' sounds like engineering, but Cable is the politician Vince Cable: supporting Cable is PRO VINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A province can be a field of activity or responsibility, as in 'that is not my sphere'.

clue.text: Flush nitrogen in reaction

indicators.note: the nitrogen symbol sits inside the word for reaction

parts.note: to get a rise out of someone is to provoke a reaction
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: nitrogen is flushed through during a reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush something is to wash it through with water, which is to rinse it.

clue.text: Switch stance on gender identity?

indicators.note: on places the stance word after the gender identity word

parts.note: trans describes a gender identity different from that assigned at birth
a pose is a stance or posture

explanation.surface: A question about someone changing their position on gender identity.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the stance comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpose is to switch things around, interchanging their order or positions.

clue.text: Six wheels or one brought in for service?

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A garage question: is it the six-wheeler, or another vehicle, that has come in for a service?
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a car's maintenance, but here it is a church service; a clergyman is brought in to take one.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest is the person who leads a church service.

clue.text: Perhaps purge rolls without enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: a whimsical reading: rolls (registers) after a purge might be left with no list at all

explanation.surface: A purge of the membership rolls carried out half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless describes someone lacking energy or interest, i.e. lethargic and apathetic.

clue.text: Very smooth, swanky ride, say, as it's made over inside

indicators.note: the example abbreviation and rearranged words go within the posh car

parts.note: a limo is a luxurious car to ride in
EG, for example, means say

indicators.note: made over means remade, so the letters of as it's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A posh car ride is very smooth because it has been refurbished inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made over' rearranges the letters of 'as it's' into ATISS, and 'inside' places that with the abbreviation for say within the posh car.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction meaning as smoothly and connectedly as possible, the superlative of legato.

clue.text: North America's to zap man with many court appearances

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America, with S for the possessive
to tase is to zap someone with a stun gun

explanation.surface: An American policing story: a man with a long criminal record gets stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court appearances' suggests trials, but Ilie Nastase was a Romanian tennis star who played on court many times.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilie Nastase, a former world number one tennis player, appeared on tennis courts many times.

clue.text: We will silence more than one comedian, maybe

definitions.meaning: people who gag others, stopping them speaking
people who tell gags, i.e. jokers

explanation.surface: A threat by a group to shut up a lot of comedians.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who gag are both silencers (gag the mouth) and joke-tellers (crack gags).

clue.text: Limit small space below second property

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts the small space under the rest

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic property
an en is a printer's space half the width of an em

explanation.surface: Landlord language: a small room below a second-home property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' puts EN, the printer's small space, under S + TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to restrict or confine, so it means to limit.

clue.text: A bighead lacking any aspiration, the man was duly rewarded with time

indicators.note: an aspiration is an H sound, so every H is dropped

parts.note: he got his means he got what he deserved

explanation.surface: A swaggering man finally gets his comeuppance, given time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition but is the breathed H sound; 'lacking any aspiration' drops both Hs from HE GOT HIS, leaving EGOTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone conceited and self-absorbed, which is what a bighead is.

clue.text: Spin one observed in nucleus of fluorine, atomic number 9

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 9 down, a region of a country

indicators.note: a spin turns things round, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the letter for one is seen inside the centre of fluorine
the nucleus is the core, so only the centre letters of fluorine are used

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
at no is the standard abbreviation for atomic number

explanation.surface: Physics jargon about the spin of a particle in a fluorine nucleus, whose atomic number is 9.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is not fluorine's atomic number but a cross-reference to 9 down. 'observed in' puts I inside OR, then AT NO follows and 'Spin' reverses OIRATNO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian province, so it is an example of the answer to 9 down.

clue.text: Altruist hasn't succeeded with a change in name

indicators.note: says one letter is missing from the selfless person's letters
the remaining letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A selfless person, having failed, changes name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' removes S from ALTRUIST, and 'with a change' rearranges ALTRUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Titular means holding a title only, existing in name but without real power.

clue.text: Here's some wordless singing involving soprano, contralto and alto?

definitions.text: Here's some wordless singing involving soprano, contralto and alto?

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the voice letters go inside the singing

parts.note: la la is singing without words

explanation.surface: A description of a venue where vocalists of every range warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' wraps LA LA round S, C and A. The whole clue also describes the place: Milan's opera house hosts such singers.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous opera house in Milan, a place where sopranos, contraltos and altos sing.

clue.text: Ordinary brook by A-road

parts.note: to brook something is to put up with or stand it
A plus RD, the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: An everyday stream running beside a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brook' looks like a stream but is the verb meaning tolerate. An A-road is a British main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Standard means normal or usual, i.e. ordinary.

clue.text: Cold food provided by Jesus himself

indicators.note: the letters are supplied by the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A biblical miracle: chilled food supplied by Jesus personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided by' points into JESUS HIMSELF, which holds SUSHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, served cold.

clue.text: Bag from fringes of Carnaby Street

indicators.note: fringes are edges, so the first and last letters of each word are used

explanation.surface: A handbag bought on the edge of a famous London shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fringes of' takes CY and ST. Carnaby Street is a London fashion street.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac or pouch in the body, so a bag in the medical sense.

clue.text: Former riding zone is risky, hero getting thrown

indicators.note: being thrown, as from a horse, scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider warns that an area is dangerous after a hero is thrown from his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riding' suggests horses, but the Ridings were the historic divisions of this English county. 'getting thrown' rearranges RISKY HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county was divided into three Ridings until 1974, so it was a zone made of ridings.

clue.text: Runner? Nearly do one!

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: do one is British slang for go away, as is skip

explanation.surface: A blunt order to a jogger: almost time to clear off!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' cuts the last letter from SKIP. 'Do one' is British slang for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is one of the long blades a sledge or skier runs on, so it is a runner.

clue.text: Delirious, at home with a clubber's pill

parts.note: in means at home
an E, i.e. a tablet of ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone babbling at home after taking a pill from a night out clubbing.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so a clubber's pill is AN E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe senseless talk or behaviour, inane meaning silly and empty-headed.

clue.text: Flat 20 cents to include new item that's charged, not quite everything

indicators.note: the coins phrase takes in the new letter

parts.note: two dimes make twenty US cents
an ion is an electrically charged particle

indicators.note: not quite means one letter short, so the end is lost

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Buying an electrical item for twenty cents leaves almost nothing in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: A dime is a US ten-cent coin. 'to include' is the container signal; 'charged' means electrically charged; 'not quite' drops the final letter of the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Having length and width but no depth, i.e. flat, literally or figuratively shallow.
